newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Merger talk sparks flurry in Gas.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Merger talk sparks flurry in Gas.

text.p: Rumours that Shell Transport is poised to launch a bid for British Gas reemerged in the weekend press and sparked a flurry of activity in British Gas options on Monday, dealers said.
The Sunday Telegraph said Shell approached British Gas with plans for a 40 billion stg merger, which drove the shares to a six-month high.

By 1248 GMT, the shares were up 14-1/2p to 223-1/2p on volume of more than 21.5 million, placing them on London's most active list. Some 5,800 lots changed hands in British Gas options with more than half the trading session over.
Volume in British Gas puts was almost two-and-a-half times that in calls, with nearly sixty percent of total volume in the December 200 puts and March 200 puts.
Dealers said a major brokerage bought at least 1,000 December 200 puts and other big brokerage bought 1,000 March 200 puts.
Dealers reckoned bulls were buying British Gas shares and out-of-the-money puts as protection. Existing holders probably also were buying puts to hedge their shares, they said.
Some of the smaller options deals were speculative, however.
"This is the resurgence of an old story and everyone has their view on it," said one dealer. "There were a few punts out there."
Trading in other stock options was sparse, dealers said.
Much of the day's trading in other equity options was linked to rollover with the November contracts set to expire on Wednesday, they said. --Debra Sherman, London newsroom +44 171 542 4026
